extracted.intended_audience: federal agency records officers, legal counsel, and individuals seeking access/correction of records under the Privacy Act/FOIA
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulations describing procedures, rights, and agency responsibilities for requests for access, amendment, accountings, disclosures, appeals, fees, security, and preservation of records under the Privacy Act (and interaction with FOIA) for agencies such as ACUS, the President's Commission on White House Fellowships, and the National Commission on Military, National, and Public Service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of requests
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of a request, the agency ordinarily will send an acknowledgment letter to the requester that will confirm the requester’s agreement to pay fees under § 304.21(c) and provide an assigned request number for further reference. In some cases, the agency may seek further information or clarification from the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should promptly acknowledge receipt, confirm fee agreement and assign a request number; may request clarifying information when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting requests for access
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the agency makes a determination to grant a request for access in whole or in part, it will notify the requester in writing, inform of any fee charged under § 304.27, and disclose records promptly on payment of any applicable fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If request made in person, agency may disclose directly in a manner not unreasonably disruptive and should make a written record of the grant. If requester is accompanied by another person, requester must authorize in writing any discussion of the records in the other's presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse determinations — definition and notice content
rubrics_metrics.description: Adverse determinations (denials) include withholding any requested record in whole or part; determination that a requested record does not exist or cannot be located; determination that requested item is not a Privacy Act record; determination on disputed fee matters; and denial of expedited treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification letter must include (1) the name and title/position of the person responsible for the denial; (2) a brief statement of the reason(s) for the denial, including any Privacy Act exemption(s) applied; and (3) a statement that the denial may be appealed under § 304.24(a) and a description of the requirements of § 304.24(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals from adverse determinations — filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If dissatisfied with an adverse determination, you may appeal in writing (email or letter) to the Chairman; appeal must be received within 60 days of the date of the denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal should provide reasons and supporting information why the initial determination was incorrect, clearly identify the particular determination (including assigned request number if known). For quickest handling of mailed appeals, mark envelope 'Privacy Act Appeal'. Chairman or designee will act on appeal; ordinarily will not act if litigation has been filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal decisions — content and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision on appeal will be made in writing. A decision affirming an adverse determination will include a brief statement of the reason(s) for the affirmance, including any exemption applied, and will inform the requester of Privacy Act provisions for court review. If reversed or modified, requester will be notified in writing and the request will be reprocessed accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must issue reasoned written appeal decisions and follow through with reprocessing when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to appeal before court review
rubrics_metrics.description: As a general rule, to seek court review of any adverse determination or denial, you must first appeal it under the agency’s appeal procedures (e.g., § 304.24(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals should use administrative appeals before initiating litigation except where exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for amendment or correction — content
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for amendment/correction should identify each particular record in question, state the amendment or correction desired, and state why you believe the record is not accurate, relevant, timely, or complete. You may submit documentation you think helpful and should state if the same record is maintained in more than one system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the same procedures as requests for access (§ 304.21) when making amendment requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency response timelines for amendment requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Within ten business days of receiving your request for amendment or correction, the agency will send a written acknowledgment of receipt. The agency will promptly notify you whether your request is granted or denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If granted in whole or part, agency will describe the amendment/correction and advise of the right to obtain a copy of the corrected or amended record. If denied, agency letter will state reasons and appeal procedures including name and business address of the official who will act on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals of amendment denials and time for action
rubrics_metrics.description: You may appeal a denial of amendment or correction the same manner as a denial of access (see § 304.24(a)). The agency will ordinarily act on the appeal within 30 business days except that the Chairman may extend time for good cause shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appeal denied, agency will advise of right to file a Statement of Disagreement and of right to court review under the Privacy Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements of Disagreement — form and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: If appeal is denied in whole or part, you have the right to file a Statement of Disagreement stating your reasons for disagreeing. Statements must be concise, clearly identify each part of any record disputed, and should be no longer than one typed page for each fact disputed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency will place the Statement in the system of records where the disputed record is maintained, mark the disputed record to indicate the Statement has been filed and exactly where it may be found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of amendment/correction to prior recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 business days of the amendment or correction of a record, the agency will notify all persons, organizations, or agencies to which it previously disclosed the record (where an accounting of that disclosure was made) that the record has been amended or corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If individual filed a Statement of Disagreement, agency will append a copy to the disputed record whenever disclosed and may append a concise statement of its reasons for denying the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records not subject to amendment or correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain records are not subject to amendment/correction: (1) transcripts of testimony given under oath or written statements made under oath; (2) transcripts of grand jury proceedings, judicial proceedings, or quasi-judicial proceedings which are the official record of those proceedings; and (3) any other record that originated with the courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must identify and exclude these categories from amendment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for accounting of disclosures — content
rubrics_metrics.description: You may request an accounting of any disclosure made by the agency of any record about you; the accounting contains the date, nature, and purpose of each disclosure, as well as the name and address of the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should identify each particular record and be made in writing following procedures in § 304.21.

rubrics_metrics.name: When accountings are not required
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency is not required to provide accountings where they relate to disclosures for which accountings are not required to be kept (disclosures to officers/employees of the agency and disclosures required under FOIA) or disclosures made to law enforcement agencies for authorized activities in response to written requests specifying portion of the record and the law enforcement activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must apply these exceptions when responding to accounting requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for duplication under the Privacy Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency will charge fees for duplication of records under the Privacy Act in the same way it charges duplication fees under § 304.9 of subpart A. No search or review fee may be charged for any record under the Privacy Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may charge only duplication fees (as prescribed); may not charge search/review fees for Privacy Act records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of court-ordered disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: When a record pertaining to an individual is required to be disclosed by a court order, the agency will make reasonable efforts to provide notice to the individual within a reasonable time after receipt of the order; if the order is not public, notice is given only after the order becomes public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice mailed to last known address and will contain a copy of the order and description of the information disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of emergency disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon disclosing a record pertaining to an individual under compelling circumstances affecting health or safety, the agency will notify that individual of the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice mailed to last known address must state nature of information disclosed; recipient; date of disclosure; and the compelling circumstances justifying the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security of systems of records — administrative and physical controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency will have administrative and physical controls to prevent unauthorized access to systems of records, prevent unauthorized disclosure, and prevent physical damage or destruction. Stringency corresponds to sensitivity of records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum controls must ensure: records protected from public view; storage area supervised during business hours; records inaccessible to unauthorized persons outside business hours; and records not disclosed to unauthorized persons in any form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictive procedures for access
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency will implement practices and procedures that restrict access to records to only those individuals within the agency who must have access in order to perform their duties and that prevent inadvertent disclosure of records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must operationalize need-to-know and safeguards to prevent inadvertent disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract requirements for record systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Any approved contract for the operation of a record system will contain appropriate requirements issued by the General Services Administration to ensure compliance with the Privacy Act for that record system. The contracting officer is responsible for ensuring contractor compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts operating systems of records must incorporate GSA-issued terms to protect Privacy Act obligations and the contracting officer must enforce them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and collection of social security numbers — notice and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees authorized to collect information must be aware that individuals may not be denied rights/benefits for refusing to provide SSNs unless collection is authorized by statute or regulation issued prior to 1975. Individuals must be informed before providing SSNs (or other info) whether providing is mandatory/voluntary; any statutory/regulatory authority authorizing collection; principal purposes for which information is intended to be used; routine uses; and effects of not providing the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requested on a form, the informing requirements must be set forth on the form or a separate form the individual can retain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee standards of conduct regarding records
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency will inform employees of Privacy Act provisions including disclosure restrictions and civil/criminal penalties. Unless otherwise permitted, employees must collect and maintain only information relevant and necessary; collect directly from individuals when information may result in adverse determinations; inform individuals as required by § 304.31(b); ensure systems have public notice; maintain records with accuracy, relevance, timeliness, completeness; make reasonable efforts prior to dissemination to ensure accuracy/relevance/timeliness/completeness (except disclosures to agencies or under FOIA); not maintain records describing First Amendment exercise except in limited circumstances; maintain required accountings; maintain and use records with care to prevent unauthorized/inadvertent disclosure; and notify appropriate officials of any record the Privacy Act does not permit the agency to maintain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are mandatory conduct standards for employees handling systems of records to ensure legal compliance and fairness to individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of records relating to requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency will preserve all correspondence pertaining to requests received under this subpart, as well as copies of all requested records, until disposition or destruction is authorized by title 44 or NARA General Records Schedule 14. Records will not be disposed of while subject to a pending request, appeal, or lawsuit under the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must retain request materials and copies until applicable retention schedules allow disposition and when no pending matters exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: No entitlement to services beyond Privacy Act rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this subpart shall be construed to entitle any person, as of right, to any service or to the disclosure of any record to which such person is not entitled under the Privacy Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations do not create additional rights beyond statutory entitlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: System of records notice and notification procedures (White House Fellowships Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission’s system of records is listed annually in the Federal Register. Any person wishing to know whether a system contains a record pertaining to them may appear in person or write to the Commission's Administrative Officer; requests are recommended to be in writing. Requests by others must state relationship, and will not be honored unless made by the individual or the individual's legal guardian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission will acknowledge requests within 10 working days and normally notify existence/non-existence within 30 working days. No special identity verification required to ask whether a system pertains to an individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for access to records (White House Fellowships Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may request review by appearing at Commission office or writing to Administrative Officer. Commission will strive to make the record available within 15 working days or inform the requester of the need for additional identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-person reasonable identification (employment ID, driver's license, credit cards) normally accepted. Charges are $0.10 per photocopy page; no charge unless computed charge would exceed $3 per request or related series; if fee in excess of $25 required requester notified and fee must be tendered before copying. Individuals will not be denied access to records pertaining to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of records — procedural details (White House Fellowships Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for amendment must be in writing to Administrative Officer; signature sufficient identification; request must contain exact description of items to be amended and specific reasons and birthdate for verification. Administrative Officer will acknowledge within 10 working days (unless processed within period) and notify within 30 days whether request granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendment appropriate (record is relevant/necessary to accomplish purpose and as accurate/timely/complete as reasonably necessary), agency will change record, advise requester that change made within 30 days, and after accountings notify prior recipients. If denied, agency will advise within 30 days with specific reasons and inform of right to review by Director within 30 days. Director will independently review using same criteria; if Director denies, actions include notifying reasons, right to file concise Statement of Disagreement, annotating records, providing statement to prior recipients after accounting, and informing of right to judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of records to others (White House Fellowships Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records subject to the Privacy Act that are requested by any person other than the individual will not be made available except: (a) circulated to appropriate officials incident to placing Fellows in work assignments; (b) an accounting of disclosures will be indicated on the record and is available to the individual on written request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit disclosures to authorized operational needs and maintain accountings accessible to individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and basic procedural scope (National Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations define terms (business day, Chair, Commission, Commission system, General Counsel, individual, Privacy Act) and state that rules apply to records retrieved by name or identifying number and establish procedures by which individuals may determine if a system contains records about them, gain access, and request correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions set the scope and applicability of the Commission's Privacy Act procedures and should be consulted when applying the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for accessing records (National Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may request notification if a named system contains records pertaining to you and to review such records by writing to the Office of the General Counsel or scheduling an in-person appointment. Requests should be in writing and identify the Commission system(s) involved. Requests for records are treated as requests under both the Privacy Act and FOIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access provided if identification requirements (§ 426.105) are satisfied and records are releasable. Only one copy of each requested record will be supplied per the fee schedule. Commission will comply promptly with in-person scheduled requests when records are immediately available, and will acknowledge within 10 business days mailed or personal requests for records not immediately available and provide information promptly thereafter.
